adjudication.mathematical correctness: UPHELD as scored. The delegate performed checkable arithmetic (log2 band spacing, Bjorklund gap multisets, onset counts, LCM-vs-duration, E(k,n) argument order, Tonnetz interval adjacency) and its findings reproduce. It also CREDITED one ring as correct (S05-A, E(5,13) gaps 2,3,2,3,3 = a rotation of 3,2,3,2,3), which overturns an earlier hand-check by the orchestrator that had called it wrong.
adjudication.accessibility: PARTIALLY VACATED. The axis conflated two claims. (a) 'no accessibility annotation; icon-only controls unlabelled' scores an un-annotated raster against docs/15 S7, which the spec explicitly defers to the annotation pass ('include visible accessibility-friendly labels for icon-only controls IN ANNOTATION VERSIONS'). Not a defect of these mockups. (b) 'sourceStatus and mappingStage carry no non-colour encoding; derivation and audio rely on coloured chips' is real, in scope, and substantively true. The reject stands only on (b).
adjudication.S8 handoff gate: NOT A DEFECT. Pixels cannot supply a component mapping, an interaction description, a token-deviation record, or a responsive rule. docs/15 S8 states these are the conditions a mockup must LATER satisfy to become implementation-authoritative; their absence in a raster is the expected state, not a finding.

defects: Mathematical correctness fails: the displayed formula f(t) = sin(2pi * 2^(t/12) * t + phi3) does not produce a clean exponential octave progression. S01.screenNotes: S01 has no requiredStates array in screens.json. All three visibly cover the core library items and preserve the no-project shell better than they cover S6/S8 proof. None visibly shows a budget/error state, an accessibility annotation, responsive rule, interaction behavior, or a complete non-color-only treatment for every semanticStates axis. A and C use Tonnetz-looking lattices without verifiable fifth/third semantics; B additionally renders an E(5,8) preview with four visible pulses rather than five.
S01.recommendationReason: A-instrument is the strongest visual/library-shell direction: it is restrained, dense, plausibly implementable, and clearest on selected project plus material treatment. It is still rejected as supplied because its Tonnetz math is not verifiable and its accessibility/S8 handoff evidence is absent.

S02.screenNotes: All three visibly provide the three S02 required states and a dark instrument-style shell, transport, collapsed graph drawer, timeline, material legend, and non-hue material-kind cues. All three nevertheless reject: each makes a checkable logarithmic-tempo claim while rendering the non-logarithmic 60/90/120/180/240 sequence at near-equal spacing; none visibly provides source-status or mapping-stage encodings, provenance/evaluation/error-budget evidence, or an accessibility annotation. S8 conditions requiring described interaction, accessibility annotation, and responsive rule/paired mockup are not fulfilled by any single image.
S02.recommendationReason: A-instrument is the closest visual basis for the required compact professional Explore shell: it keeps the inspector collapsed, makes the required badges/statuses readable, and most clearly applies distinct material textures. It remains rejected until the logarithmic scale is corrected and the missing semantic/accessibility, provenance, budget/error, and S8 handoff evidence are supplied.

S03.screenNotes: All three visibly preserve the dark instrument shell, a working transport, material legend, mapping stages, evaluation evidence, a timeline, and a separated experimental area. All three omit a visible error/budget state and lack the non-pixel artifacts required by S8: accessibility annotation, described interaction behavior, and paired/written responsive behavior. A and B must be rejected for visible mathematical contradictions; C is the only variant without one found in the rendered values.
S03.recommendationReason: C-spatial is the only variant that passes all three reject axes and its displayed exponential octave relation is numerically coherent. It still needs a clearly labelled rendered unwrapped view, explicit non-colour selection treatment, error/budget state, and S8 annotation/interaction/responsive handoff artifacts.

S04.screenNotes: S04 has no requiredStates entry in screens.json. All three images visibly deliver a dark desktop shell, concentric rings, four tracks, a timeline, a material legend, a collapsed graph drawer, a selection treatment, provenance/evaluation surfaces, and all four material-kind textures. All three omit any visible error/budget state and the S8 artifacts that cannot be inferred from pixels: interaction description, accessibility annotation, and paired/written responsive behavior. Mathematical correctness rejects A for its contradictory cycle duration, B for its inverted E(k,n) notation and non-Euclidean formula, and C for a false LCM plus an E(5,16) ring rendered with 16 onsets.
S04.recommendationReason: A is the least damaged visual direction: it has the clearest dense creative-tool hierarchy and the strongest cross-surface selection. It is still rejected and must correct the composite-cycle duration, add visible error/budget treatment, and complete the S8 accessibility, interaction, and responsive handoff evidence before use.

S05.screenNotes: All three visibly satisfy S05's three required states and use a dark, compact studio vocabulary. All three nevertheless fail the S8 handoff gate from pixels alone: no interaction specification, accessibility annotation, responsive pair/rule, or token-deviation record is present. All three also omit visible error/budget handling and do not make every semanticStates axis independently non-color-only. A and C have E(5,13) claims, while B has E(5,8); B and C visibly contradict their stated Euclidean parameters, and A's Tonnetz contains a visible C-to-F# tritone adjacency.
S05.recommendationReason: B is still rejected because its E(5,8) geometry is mathematically wrong and it has no accessibility annotation, but it is the only variant that visibly distinguishes all four material kinds with labels, texture, and glyphs while exposing a usable provenance/evaluation surface. Correct its five-onset ring to rotated E(5,8) steps 1,3,4,6,7 before using it as a basis.

S06.screenNotes: All variants visibly cover the four S06 required states and use strong non-color material-kind textures. All three nevertheless fail the S6 reject gate: their Euclidean claims are either contradicted by identical step markers (C) or not countably rendered (A, B); sourceStatus and full non-color semantic-state coverage are absent; and no accessibility annotation is visible. Each also lacks a visible S8-authoritative handoff package.
S06.recommendationReason: B is the least bad foundation because its selection, provenance, dependency categories, keyboard route, and material lineage are clearest. It remains rejected until the mathematical renderings are made countable/correct, garbled text is replaced, accessibility is annotated, and the S8 handoff evidence is supplied.

S07.screenNotes: All three make every S07 required state visibly findable and use useful texture/line/glyph treatments for the material kinds. All three nevertheless reject: each claims a Euclidean rhythm while rendering the wrong number of onsets, and none includes the accessibility annotation, icon labels, responsive rule, component mapping, token-deviation record, or behavioral specification required for S8 implementation-authoritative handoff. No text is visibly garbled or misspelled; the defects are semantic and mathematical, not OCR noise.
S07.recommendationReason: A-instrument is the least compromised visual base: it has the clearest cross-surface selection chain, the most complete source-status/evidence treatment, and the strongest compact instrument shell. It remains rejected until its E(7,12) ring is corrected to seven Euclidean onsets and the absent S8 accessibility, behavior, responsive, component-mapping, and token-deviation evidence is supplied.
